title: Server-Side Coroutines
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of server-side coroutines using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates server-side coroutines.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Server-Side Coroutines** as part of **Kotlin for Backend and Server-Side Development**. A coroutine can suspend without blocking the thread, but it still runs on threads; scope lifetime, dispatcher choice, cancellation, and shared state remain important. Use the subtopics—Asynchronous Request Processing, Cancellation and Timeouts, Database and Network Concurrency—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Backend code handles untrusted requests and persistent data. Validation, authorization, predictable errors, and operational checks must happen on the server.

items.title: Asynchronous Request Processing
items.text: Asynchronous Request Processing is one part of server-side coroutines. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Cancellation and Timeouts
items.text: Cancellation and Timeouts depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This example requires kotlinx-coroutines-core (and the matching Flow APIs where used). Run it in a Kotlin/JVM Gradle project; do not paste it into a plain browser preview.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
